This classic oak well bucket was first taken from a farm in southern Indiana in 1925. The schools are connected by a chain, and the series history is recorded by adding brass "I" and "P" links to the handle after each game. TCU (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) visit No. 9 Texas Tech (10-1, 7-1) in Week 13's Battle for the Saddle on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, Texas (8 p.m. ET, ESPN). Spread prediction: TCU Horned Frogs +14.5 Total prediction: Under 47.5 Prop: TCU +3.5 first quarter TOP PICK TCU vs Texas Tech spread prediction: TCU +14.5 I'm fading the move toward the Texas Tech Red Raiders now that the spread has crossed a key number. I'll take TCU Horned Frogs +14.5, down to +12.5 . The Red Raiders opened as 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi. However, the line movement feels driven more by perception than new information . TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . More importantly, the Red Raiders rank 77th nationally in third-down conversion rate and 108th in red-zone scoring rate . That's a problem when laying nearly two touchdowns because converting in high-leverage situations is how favorites build a margin. TCU vs Texas Tech live odds movement TCU vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 47.5 The Under 47.5 is tradable down to 45.5 . Texas Tech can overwhelm TCU, so the Horned Frogs need to turn this game into a rock fight to have any shot at an upset. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. Meanwhile, both offensive lines struggle with pass protection and both defenses have high sack rates, opening the door for drive-killing sacks. TCU vs Texas Tech combo I'm essentially investing in Texas Tech winning ugly, which wouldn't be the worst outcome for a team with legitimate College Football Playoff hopes. If TCU can avoid giving the Red Raiders short fields, Texas Tech might have to chew up a significant amount of clock to build a comfortable lead. Furthermore, a two-score deficit wouldn't necessarily force the Horned Frogs to abandon their offensive game plan early, especially if their defense is keeping them within striking distance. TCU has finished nine of its 11 first quarters trailing by no more than three points this season. Interim head coach Andy Avalos could also dial up a few trick plays early. What does he have to lose? Between TCU's stout run defense and Texas Tech's struggles on passing downs , this has the makings of a slow start for the Red Raiders. What's at stake? The TCU Horned Frogs parted ways with head coach Sonny Dykes on Sunday following Saturday's loss to No. 2 Utah , which marked the Frogs' final home game of the season. Defensive coordinator Andy Avalos will take over as interim head coach as TCU looks to navigate the coaching change and secure bowl eligibility. Thursday's Thanksgiving matchup represents the Frogs' final opportunity to clinch a bowl berth. The game also gives Avalos his first opportunity to make an impression and help TCU finish the season on a positive note despite the changes surrounding the program. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig did not suit up against No. 2 Utah, despite expectations he would play following last Tuesday's news conference. Sophomore Adam Schobel made his first start of the season. While it was a rough first half for the quarterback, Schobel connected on a few plays to help TCU cut into a 17-0 deficit. He finished the game completing 15 of 31 passes for 106 yards with two interceptions and added 30 yards rushing on 12 carries. TCU struggled to find consistent offense against Utah, particularly when it came to sustaining drives and moving the ball through the air. The Frogs will need to be more efficient against a Texas Tech defense that has helped the Red Raiders put together a 10-1 season. Craig's potential return could boost the Frogs' offense. His experience and ability to make plays with his arm could help TCU establish a rhythm early, but his ankle injury could also limit what the offense is able to do. If Schobel plays, he'll at least have the benefit of one start under his belt. When Texas Tech has the ball Texas Tech enters Thursday's matchup riding a four-game winning streak and remains undefeated at home. The Red Raiders have been playing with confidence and will look to take advantage of a TCU team navigating a coaching change and uncertainty at quarterback. Texas Tech has been productive offensively, averaging 444.4 yards of total offense per game. Its balanced attack could present a challenge for TCU's defense, which allowed Utah to score three touchdowns in the fourth quarter. The Red Raiders are looking to earn a spot in the Big 12 Championship game and make the College Football Playoff . Tech will need to be disciplined and lean on starting quarterback Thomas Castellanos , who has thrown for 985 yards, 14 touchdowns and three interceptions this season. While the Frogs will look to rally behind Avalos and fight for bowl eligibility, the uncertainly following Dykes' departure and Craig's status at quarterback will make it too difficult to overcome Texas Tech's momentum and home-field advantage. picks.blurb: Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. home.blurb: Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. home.headline: Joey McGuire’s declaration puts Texas Tech above even 2025 CFP team
home.blurb: The Texas Tech football team is hoping to return to the College Football Playoff this season. The Red Raiders are in a solid position to do that, with just one loss on the season. Texas Tech head coach Joey McGuire is making a bold declaration about this year’s squad. “I don’t think I’ve ever been more proud of a team in my career than this team right here,” McGuire said after defeating TCU, per On3. Texas Tech is now headed back to the Big 12 championship game. The Red Raiders finished the regular season with a 11-1 record, and 8-1 in the Big 12. The team’s lone loss of the season was to Cincinnati on the road. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I can’t wait to get back to Arlington,” McGuire said, per the school. “It’s my second-favorite place to play. It’s going to be a home game next week for us.” Texas Tech picked up their 11th win of the season against TCU, 48-27. This Red Raiders team has been very difficult to beat in Lubbock under McGuire’s tenure. “The Red Raiders have won a school-record 15 consecutive games at home, the second-longest active streak in college football to Ohio’s 18,” the school announced. Texas Tech now plays an undefeated Utah team in the Big 12 title game. Utah crushed West Virginia on Friday night , to finish their regular season at 12-0. “The job’s not done yet, so it’s not going to be too much celebrating,” Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos said after beating TCU. “We’re not just looking for that next one.” Texas Tech and Utah will play on Friday December 4 for the conference championship. picks.headline: Florida Gators at Florida State Preview: How Do Gators Match Up vs. Seminoles?
picks.blurb: Florida Gators at Florida State Preview: How Do Gators Match Up vs. Seminoles? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM GATORS FB SI.COM GATORS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS For the third time ever, the Florida Gators will face the Florida State Seminoles on Black Friday at Doak Campbell Stadium. Florida State has had a very underwhelming season, sitting at 5-6 after firing head coach Mike Norvell a few weeks ago and just announcing they'll hire Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schuman as the next head coach. This will be the 70th all-time matchup between these two in-state rivals, with Florida leading the series 39-28-2 all time. The Gators are looking for their third straight victory in the rivalry. Florida has the opportunity in this one to not only win eight regular-season games for the first time since 2020, but also keep their counterparts from making a bowl game. It may not have been a pretty last couple of weeks for the Gators, but a chance to finish the season winning three straight, building momentum for the future, is a good starting point for year one under a new head coach. On the other hand, the Seminoles are coming off arguably their worst loss of the season at home, losing by 18 points to a 5-6 NC State team. Although, the Seminoles are 2-1 since firing head coach Mike Norvell, with Rock Stockstill at the helm. A look at Florida State The Seminoles have dealt with a lot of injuries to key players like wide receiver Duce Robinson, running back Ousman Kromah, and multiple defensive players, including team sack leader Rylan Kennedy, plus inconsistent play this season. Offensively, the Seminoles are headlined by Auburn transfer quarterback Ashton Daniels. Daniels is a volatile quarterback accounting for 27 total touchdowns this year (14 passing, 13 rushing) and 14 interceptions. Daniels is a good athlete who can make explosive plays through the air and with his legs but is prone to costly mistakes. “Yeah, I think the quarterback's talented,” Jon Sumrall said. “He's athletic. He's played a lot of college football. He's a playmaker. He can extend plays, great plays with his legs. He can make all the throws. Their receiving core to me, is really scary. “I think this No. 8, 7, 15, all three of those guys I think are big-time players. The 8 guy, No. 8, Danzy's got elite top-end speed. I think 7, he's got a basketball background. He's a very natural, efficient mover. And then 15's got really good ball skills. I know they've been banged up a little bit at running back. That's been a challenge for them.” Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. No purchase necessary. 50 U.S./D.C. 18+. The College Football Playoff (CFP) is not a sponsor or administrator of this contest. As Sumrall said, their top playmakers are receievrs Micahi Danzy, Jayvan Boggs and Jansen Lopez. Last week against NC State, the Noles were missing their top four running backs, so expect a more pass-heavy attack from FSU. The 'Noles rank around league average in the ACC in points per game with 27.5 and total yards per game at 385.3. Defensively, Florida State is towards the bottom third of the league in total yards per game at 407.7 and points per game at 26.6. The Seminoles' rush defense also ranks in the bottom three in the conference. The Seminole defense is led by linebacker Chris Jones, who leads the team in all tackle categories, and defensive back Ashland Barker who is a long, lengthy corner who is tied for the team lead in interceptions. The Gators offensively need to get the ground game working for numerous reasons. Jadan Baugh is 20 yards short of 1,000 rushing yards ; Florida State's run defense is arguably their worst unit on their team, and in the Gators four losses this season Baugh has averaged a mere 36.3 rushing yards per game. Defensively, the Gators have to contain quarterback Ashton Daniels and force him into tough throwing windows while also limiting his escapability, which he loves to do to extend drives and create explosive plays. Sumrall highlights how important it is to win in-state rivalry games while also how it helps with winning in-state recruiting battles. "You want to win the state,” Sumrall said. “That's a big deal. I have a lot of respect for everybody we play in-state, or even the ones we don't. But you want to win the in-state battles, whether it be on the field or in recruiting, whatever. We compete every day, and so it's a huge deal. “Coach Meyer texted me maybe around the Texas game, and just said, 'Hey, finish this thing strong all the way down the stretch in November. Recruit the roster you need to recruit to build this thing.' And so he emphasized the reason to finish in November in a lot of ways, and getting some momentum as you go into the offseason as you build for the future, and this game is a big part of it. “And in-state rivalries, they matter. Anybody that says just another game, I don't buy into that. It's not just another game; it's an in-state rivalry. Those are different, but the world we live in are all big because we play in the SEC, and week in, week out, they're all big games, and they're all challenging games. This is one that means something to so many people "Because the in-state rivalry component, it is a bragging-rights in-state game, which does matter." The Gators cannot afford to overlook a disappointing Florida State squad as kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. EST this afternoon on ABC. Pictured: Florida Gators RB Jadan Baugh, QB Aaron Philo and OL Harrison Moore Road ToCFB · Action Network Fri, November 27, 2026 at 12:15 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators take on the Florida State Seminoles in Tallahassee, Florida. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. EST on ABC. Florida is favored by 6.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -230. The total is set at 53.5 points. Here's my Florida vs. Florida State prediction and college football pick for Friday, November 27, 2026. Florida vs. Florida State Pick: Florida -6 (-112) My Florida St vs. Florida best bet is on the Gators against the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Florida vs Florida State Odds Florida vs Florida State point spread : Florida -6.5 (-110), Florida St +6.5 (-110) Florida vs Florida State over/under : 53.5 (-110o / -110u) Florida vs Florida State moneyline : Florida -230, Florida St +190 Florida started off the Jon Sumrall era scorching hot. Its offense seemed impossible to stop, hanging 52 on Ole Miss in Week 4. But inconsistency has been rampant across the team, with all four of Florida's losses coming by 16-plus points. Outside of that Ole Miss trouncing — a game that came off the back of a wildly emotional Rebels win over LSU — Florida has a negative point margin in SEC play. There are two big wins over Texas and Kentucky (both on the road) but also a one-score sweat over Vanderbilt at home. Florida is a mystery box each and every week. Florida's offensive line has been a root of the issue in an offense that's very much run-first. Early downs have become predictable, with the featured player being Jadan Baugh (960 yards, SEC-leading 16 rushing touchdowns). Quarterback Aaron Philo has been utilized well when healthy, rushing for almost 200 yards and three touchdowns over the past two games, and Florida converts regularly on late downs. Two major issues plague Florida's defense, and they've blown the floodgates open: it allows too many consistent chunk plays through the air and cannot get off the field on late downs. The Gators rank 125th nationally in third/fourth-down success rate (50.3%) and 121st in Passing Success Rate. Jayden Woods and Emmanuel Oyebadejo make up one of the SEC's most productive pass-rush duos, with 14 combined sacks (Oyebadejo notched two of his own last week). But when the rush isn't getting home, Florida's secondary struggles to contain production. The best of Florida gives you one of the best football teams in the country. But there's been more bad than good lately, and Florida's floor is the bottom third of the SEC. Florida State 's long nightmare is over as Mike Norvell finally got the axe. Not only that, but FSU already has its next head coach lined up: Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. But until Schumann takes over, Rick Stockstill will lead the 'Noles as interim head coach. Under Stockstill, FSU is 2-1, with one-score wins over a free-falling Pitt (lost five of its last six) and Boston College, along with a 28-10 loss to NC State last week. Not super inspiring results, to say the least. Against NC State, Florida State gained just 36% of available yards and hit the Red Zone just once (on the opening drive). It put the ball in harm's way four times, fortunately recovering both fumbles but also throwing two interceptions. Quarterback Ashton Daniels is now up to 14 picks thrown on the year, the most among FBS arms. The run game has struggled without Ousmane Kromah (out for the year with an ankle injury), and the throw game has struggled without Duce Robinson (torn ACL). Four-star freshman Amari Thomas left early last week, and Tre Wisner hasn't played since Week 10. This is an offense limping to the finish line, with a quarterback doing everything he can as his eligibility runs out. The Seminoles don't have the horses to be effective in the Gus Malzahn-esque option system. Offensive struggle usually comes with a defensive slip (see: Ohio State ). FSU hasn't played a quality offense since Miami (43 points allowed in a pair of overtimes) and Louisville (44 allowed the week before). Since then, it's been a run of injured teams that didn't have much offensive prowess to begin with. Of course, FSU is capable of getting up for one more game against bitter rival Florida. These intrastate rivalries in the Sunshine State are packed with genuine vitriol, and this roster will do everything but roll over and die, especially since a good chunk of it is still Florida-grown. Florida is a six-point road favorite this Saturday, with an over/under of 53.5. Florida has been bad as a favorite this year, posting a 2-6 ATS record with three outright losses. Meanwhile, Florida State is 4-1-1 ATS as an underdog this season. This line remained unchanged since the lookahead line posted this summer for both the total and spread. Florida State's roster has been decimated. Its top weapons are out for the remainder of the season, and the two fill-ins in the backfield are both banged up. For a run-first team, losing that kind of firepower in the backfield is a massive handicap. With the Schumann era on the doorstep and with a roster missing significant portions of its lineup, this is a game Florida State might just be happy to get over with, even if it is against an in-state rival. Favorites have covered each of the last four in this series, with Florida running away with the last two meetings. The Gators are much healthier coming into this matchup with more stability in the coaching ranks heading into 2027. This is a numbers play. Anything at +7 or better is probably a bet on FSU, while anything under is all Florida. Pick: Florida -6 (-112, DraftKings | Play to -6.5)

The Florida Gators (7-4) invade Doak Campbell Stadium to battle the Florida State Seminoles (5-6) Saturday. Florida is currently on a two-game winning streak, with victories over Kentucky and Vanderbilt. Florida State is coming off a home loss to NC State. The Gators have won two straight over the Seminoles . Broadcast Information Date: Friday, November 27, 2026 Time: 3:30 p.m. ET Location: Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee, Florida Betting Odds: Florida -6.5-point road favorite Florida started the season 4-0 under new head coach Jon Sumrall, including a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss . The Gators also beat No. 7 Texas by three points. The Florida offense is led by running back Jadan Baugh , who leads the SEC with 16 rushing touchdowns. He has rushed for 980 yards. Commanding this offense on the field is quarterback Aaron Philo. Philo has passed for 1,727 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. He has completed 70.9 percent of his passes. However, Philo has not thrown a touchdown pass in five weeks (since Oct. 10). In the win over Texas , Philo did not play. Tramell Jones started in his place, and threw for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the 27-24 victory. On defense, the player to watch is JCK Jayden Woods. Woods leads the team with seven sacks and 11 tackles for loss. He has collected 45 tackles. As a unit, the Gators are not good at getting off the field on third down. Florida has allowed opponents to convert on third down 45 percent of the time. That ranks near the bottom of the SEC. Further, Florida is not good at stopping opponents in the red zone. Teams are scoring at an 88 percent clip against the Gators inside the 20-yard line. Florida State has navigated chaos and bedlam since the firing of Mike Norvell. They won two road games and hired a new athletic director, Jeff Purinton. Then, they hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann as their new head football coach. Interim coach Rick Stockstill and interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims have coached the Seminoles to a 2-1 record after losing three straight games. Injuries have decimated the roster, especially at running back. The rushing attack falls on the shoulders of running back Zay Parks and designed runs (and not so designed) by quarterback Ashton Daniels . Parks has rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown over the last two games. Daniels leads all ACC quarterbacks with 13 rushing touchdowns. He also rushed for 459 yards. Further, Daniels leads the ACC in interceptions with 14. He has thrown for 2,515 yards, and 14 touchdowns. Daniels is 26 yards away from 3,000 total yards accounted for. On defense, linebacker Chris Jones continues to be a force on defense. Jones leads the team in tackles with 85 stops. The Seminoles have come a long way over the last few weeks. Florida State has an opportunity for a sixth win and to become bowl eligible. Just as important, they also have a chance to send Stockstill out as a winner.

Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) and Florida (7-4, 5-4 SEC) will meet for the 70th time, with Florida leading the all-time series 39-28-2, and winners of the last two matchups (40-21 in 2025 and 31-11 in 2024). FSU is 2-0 against the Gators on Fridays, winning 27-16 in 1979 and 45-38 in 2022, and the Noles have beaten five ranked SEC teams in the regular season since 2015, the most nationally among non-SEC programs. The Seminoles have started four running backs this season, including junior Zay Parks last week against NC State. Parks began his career as a walk-on and combined for 65 yards on 17 carries against Pitt and NC State, including a 9-yard touchdown on his first carry against the Wolfpack, FSU’s lone touchdown in the game. It was his second career touchdown. Meanwhile, on the Gators’ first possession Friday, running back Jadan Baugh will likely break the 1,000-yard mark for the season. Baugh already has 980 yards this season and averages 5.0 yards per carry. Baugh has recorded 8 explosive runs of 20+ yards, including runs of 75, 61, and 53 yards, and has scored 16 rushing TDs this season. UF’s Aaron Philo has firmly established himself as the starting quarterback after alternating with Tramell Jones Jr. earlier in the year. Philo enters on a two-game winning streak following victories over No. 11 Kentucky and Vanderbilt, where he completed 20 of 26 passes for 241 yards with no interceptions and added 73 rushing yards with two touchdowns. Receivers Bailey Stockton and Dallas Wilson are tied with 41 receptions each and a combined 5 receiving TDs. UF’s defense is led by linebacker Myles Graham, son of former NFL running back Earnest Graham, who leads the team with 88 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and 5.5 tackles for loss and returned a fumble 57 yards for a touchdown in last week’s win over Vanderbilt. Some other defensive players whose names we will hear mentioned are LB Aaron Chiles and DE Jayden Woods, who leads the team with 7 sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Last week against NC State, after marching 75 yards in 5 plays on their opening drive to score a touchdown, the Seminoles would only score a field goal in the second quarter, then were shut down and shut out in the second half. FSU was held to 283 total yards, lost the time-of-possession battle by over 13 minutes, and the defense gave up 464 total yards and almost 6 yards per play. Florida State shut out in the second half as Noles fall to NC State One of the few bright spots this season has been FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski, who is 27-for-27 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 12-for-12 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 27 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. For the second year in a row, the Seminoles go 5-7. UF 31, FSU 17 Jon Marchant (season record: 7-4 ) I think it’s safe to say the temporary bump from firing Mike Norvell has won off, and along with all of the injuries on offense this team is a shell of whatever it was earlier this season. The Norvell era wasn’t all bad but there was a lot of bad, and it never quite turned out the way we all wanted it too, Norvell included. I think they’ll play harder in this one similar to how they did vs Miami, but the injuries on offense will probably be too much to overcome. Again though, if there’s any takeaway from the Mike Norvell era it’s that any result, good or bad, was never off the table. Florida 31, FSU 23 Tim Scribble (season record: 7-4 ) I fear that this week’s game will be similar to last year’s result. The Florida State defense will be unable to stop UF running back Jadan Baugh. Expect a lot of yards on the ground for the Gators to officially close the Mike Norvell era. UF 35, FSU 20 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-4, ATS: 7-4) Man, I am so tired of losing rivalry games. I just don’t see how FSU will get UF off the field on third downs. And with so many injuries on offense, I don’t see how FSU will score beyond a random explosive play. The only way FSU hangs tough is by winning the turnover battle by a big margin, and that’s tough to do when your QB leads the country in INTs. UF 35, FSU 16 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-4, ATS: 3-8) Hard to shake my belief that this will be the third time in six years Florida denies FSU a bowl bid. The Gators haven’t been an incredible team all season but their highs have been much higher than Florida State’s. Florida 31, Florida State 20 Frank DNole (season record: 5-6) If you look at the Florida State vs. Florida head-to-head comparison chart above, you will notice that the Gators hold the statistical advantage over the Noles in almost every category. Normally, that might be the recipe for a Seminole defeat. However, this week we experienced a full moon that is now in the waning gibbous phase. Not only was it a full moon, but it was also a supermoon, and most importantly, it was a Full Beaver Moon (look it up). What all this means is that the Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special-teams battles because the FSU players will give 115% more effort, they will want it more, and the Noles will play with more heart than their more talented turdly opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, FFFFF 31 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 6-5, 5-6 ATS) I really can’t tell you why I’m going with this choice other than pure delusion, but I have a weird feeling about this game. Here’s a fun fact: interim coaches have gone 3-1 in the series since 2017 (well, I guess technically 3-2, since the 2017 matchup was a matchup of two interims). Two of those wins were on the UF end, but if we’re talking delusion, why not warp some stats in favor of the home team? FSU has shed two streaks (last road win, last Friday win) that were defined by a win over the Gators this season since Rick Stockstill took over, so in the interest of the rule of threes, why not finally earn bowl eligibility with a season-ending victory over the boys from Hogtown? Again, this is a feeling borne out of nothing other than an inkling, since everything on paper and on film says UF should win this one with no issues. Jaden Baugh seems to take particular joy in the rivalry, which doesn’t bode well for an FSU defense that struggles against a lot, but especially against the run. FSU is stumbling in this health-wise, the high-flying feelings of go 2-0 to the Norvell era seemingly washed away by NC State. And unless Tre Wisner has made a turnaround on being healthy, Florida State is going to have to win this on the arm of Ashton Daniels, which the cope glass-half-full way of looking at it is that he has a penchant for performing in rivalry matchups. The only non-delusional, non-anything-can-happen-in-a-rivalry-game reasons I have for thinking that FSU is capable of pulling off a win is that 1) UF has played down to its opponents all season long and 2) the Gators are vulnerable on defense, especially through the air. But brother, it’s Turkey Day, and if there’s one thing I’m thankful for, it’s me never, ever, ever, ever, ever learning my lesson. home.headline: How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State
home.blurb: Florida hasn't lost to FSU since its horrific 5-7 season in 2023 when the Seminoles were a perfect 13-0 but still missed out on the College Football Playoffs. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

picks.headline: Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions
picks.blurb: Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Wisconsin Badgers have the chance to end the 2026 campaign on a high note if they are able to take down the Minnesota Golden Gophers and move to 8-4. By no means would it be a storied season that goes down in the record books, but it should be enough to keep Fickell from any more serious conversations about his job security. That being said, all that momentum would cease if Wisconsin were to lose to Minnesota, and knowing how inconsistent Wisconsin has been this season, there aren't many things you can bank on. However, we take our best cracks at three predictions below. No. 1: Wisconsin loses the turnover battle None of these predictions will come off as hot takes by any means, but perhaps this is the most levelheaded take on this list. On the season, the Badgers sit 80th in turnover margin at -2 against FBS competition. Minnesota, on the other hand, is 14th-best in the nation at a +7 margin. No. 2 Wisconsin's rushing offense is responsible for each of their touchdowns As previously mentioned, the Badgers are inconsistent this season, and usually when the offense looks like it has something figured out, the next week it falls apart. Well, last week the Badgers' offense ran for 381 yards across 51 total carries that involved two 100+ yard runners in Colton Joseph and Darrion Dupree. That being said, Minnesota's pass defense against FBS competition ranks 35th-best in the country, allowing 196.6 yards through the air. Their rushing defense, meanwhile, sits No. 74 in the country at 154.4 yards. If Wisconsin's offense is productive, it likely comes on the ground. No. 3 The two teams do not combine for 600 yards of total offense All that needs to be said here is that the Badgers and the Gophers each have a top-50 defense against FBS competition (Wisconsin 5th, Minnesota 42nd) while also posting total offenses that rank 118th and 131st. Now it’s playing for a better bowl game (which was unthinkable a month ago, let alone at the beginning of the season). Rivalry games are still important. The Buckeyes don’t need to be told that. All they must do now is win, especially for Jeremiah Smith , Ryan Day, Julian Sayin, the support staff and Buckeye Nation. If they can’t, the season will be more than just a disaster. It will be a colossal failure, bowl game or not, and it will kill any chance of a nine-win season. It’s a must-win for Ohio State, period. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 20, Michigan 13 Ohio State is playing purely for pride, as “The Game” has been stripped of its traditional luster with both teams in uncharacteristic seasons of mediocrity. The Michigan defense is very stout, and it will make field position a premium consideration when or if Ohio State is able to get into the red zone. Even though the Ohio State defense was terrible last week at Nebraska, I have blind faith that the run defense will rebound against the Wolverines and make it more difficult for Michigan on the offensive side of the ball. The Buckeyes don't need to be impenetrable, but they do need to make projected starting quarterback Bryce Underwood beat them with the passing game, and that's been a challenge for Michigan all season. The season is not what any Ohio State wanted or expected, but I believe that the Buckeyes will end on a positive note as they await their bowl game destination. Dylan Buganski: Michigan 16, Ohio State 13 The feeling around “The Game” this year is unlike anything we have seen in the last 30 years. No playoff implications. Questions around the coaching staff on both sides. Neither team ranked in the top 15 for the first time since 1987. Yet, I expect this game to be one of the closest games we have seen in recent history between the two. Both teams come into the matchups with opposite trends, with Michigan forcing three turnovers and shocking undefeated UCLA at home and Ohio State crumbling their chances to sneak into the College Football Playoff with another defensive letdown to Nebraska. I expect an ugly, punt-filled game with both teams struggling to find first downs consistently. The difference will be the ability to win the turnover margin, which favors the Wolverines. Jeremiah Smith will still top 100 yards and find a score in this game, but Ohio State’s unfinished drives and turnovers will haunt them, leaving Michigan with opportunities to score points and make the poor season for the Buckeyes a complete nightmare, with head coach Ryan Day losing the matchup for the fifth time in six years. Michigan vs. Ohio State . Buckeyes vs. Wolverines . It's the best rivalry in all of football and it's here. But it's not the normal game. Neither team is doing anything special with its postseason plans. The Wolverines nor the Buckeyes are headed to the Big Ten title game, nor does either team have a spot in the playoff. Instead, both teams are bowl-eligible, and as bad as Michigan's season has been, a win over the Buckeyes and Ohio State will have the same record as the Wolverines this season— 7-5. But Michigan will have to play another good game in order to pull off back-to-back upsets after taking down UCLA last weekend in triple overtime. Here's how Michigan on SI sees the game going. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Savion Hiter ran for over 100 yards in the last two games, so there are some silver lining. And Ohio State's defense hasn't been good in the last four games. But the Buckeyes will have the best player on the field in Jeremiah Smith, who will be hard to defend. This game is 100% winnable for Michigan, but I haven't seen enough from the Wolverines' offense to believe they can make enough plays to pull off another upset . Final score: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 Justice Steiner This is one of the least anticipated versions of ‘The Game’ we have seen in recent memory. Ohio State is on the decline since starting QB Julian Sayin went down with an injury. But it does feel like both coaches are fighting to keep their jobs. If Michigan wants to win, they need to contain Jeremiah Smith the best they can and get Savion Hiter going in the run game. Also, continuing to get the tight ends involved like they did last week will be big for the UofM offense, something they haven’t done most of the season. Although I believe Michigan has a chance and the game will be close, I don’t trust them to pick up the win on the road. This Ohio State team is not as good as any of the iterations Michigan has played since then. The Wolverine defense is good enough to keep them in the game. Jay Hill says he has a plan for Jeremiah Smith. The plan only goes so far. At some point, Ohio State's playmakers will just make one too many plays against Michigan's defense The Wolverine offense, which was still bad last week, will struggle again as the season ends at 6-6 with a narrow Buckeye victory in Columbus. Jason B. Hirschhorn From a playoff perspective, Saturday's matchup between Michigan and Ohio State lacks juice. The Wolverines fell completely out of the playoff discourse back in October, and the Buckeyes did the same after losing three of their last four games. And yet, the 2026 edition of The Game holds tremendous stakes for both sides. With another loss, Ohio State will exceed its total from the last two years combined and tie for its most in a single season with a non-interim head coach since 2001. Such a result could cost Ryan Day his job. On the other side, Michigan needs a win to avoid finishing a non-truncated regular season with a non-winning record for the first time since the Brady Hoke era. If Kyle Whittingham has any hope of surviving 2026, he'll need the political capital that comes with a victory over the Wolverines' archrivals. If star players determine the outcome, the Buckeyes have the advantage. Superstar wideout and Heisman front-runner Jeremiah Smith provides instant offense, and even the best teams struggle to contain him. However, if the Wolverines' defense can fluster freshman quarterback Luke Fahey and come up with a key turnover or two à la Chris Bracy's acrobatic interception against UCLA, they have a chance. Ultimately, slowing down Smith long enough for Michigan's lackluster offense to capitalize on the other end seems too big of an ask. Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Game is here . Tomorrow, Michigan will face Ohio State in a game that unfortunately does not mean as much as it has for each of the last 10 years. Neither team is playing for anything significant. The Wolverines are going to be bowl eligible after last week’s win over UCLA. This week’s game is mor e about pride, and bragging rights. Those still matter, even in this day in age. Here are our predictions for The Game Jeremiah Smith is Good, not Great Jay Hill says he has a plan. That’s a good start against someone as good as Jeremiah Smith. Smith, however, is going to make plays at some point. Smith was pretty quiet in the team’s 13-10 loss to Michigan in 2024. He had just three catches for 40 yards and a touchdown last year, but the Buckeyes took the air out of the ball for most of the second half. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Wed, November 25, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The final week of what has been a disappointing regular season has arrived, as the Michigan Wolverines are hitting the road to take on the Ohio State Buckeyes in The Game. A few weeks ago, this was a day that Michigan fans were dreading, but the Wolverines are actually coming into this one with more momentum than the Buckeyes. Michigan fans finally had reason to celebrate last week, as the Wolverines knocked off previously undefeated UCLA in the Big House in triple overtime. After a difficult first ten games, senior day in Ann Arbor was a resounding success. On the other side, Ohio State is having its worst season in nearly 15 years. The Buckeyes are currently 7-4 after losing three of their last four games, and last week was an unfortunate one, as Ohio State became the first ranked team to lose to Nebraska since 2016. All in all, it has been a long time since The Game featured two teams struggling like this. The season is over for both teams, but still, it's The Game. It's going to be a battle, and here are a few bold predictions for the matchup: Savion Hiter will rush for over 150 yards Yes, you read that right. For the first time in weeks, I am making a positive prediction for the Wolverines. When they go up against a team coached by Ryan Day, anything is possible. The winner of The Game has won the rushing battle every single year for the last 24 years. If Michigan has a good day on the ground, there is a solid chance that it can pull off the upset. Savion Hiter has rushed for over 100 yards in each of Michigan's last two games, so he is playing his best ball at the right time. Last week, the Buckeyes gave up 176 rushing yards to Nebraska, and Ohio State only gained 76 yards. With Michigan's lack of a passing game, the run game needs to have a good day. Michigan will win on the last play of the game One thing about this Michigan team is it has a flair for the dramatic. In 11 games, three have ended with a score on the final play of the game to win the game. Of the other eight, six have been one-score games. There's a solid chance that this is going to be another close one. There have already been three games that ended with a score on the final play, so why not one more? I think this is going to be another close one between these two bitter rivals, and Michigan will win in dramatic fashion one more time. Michigan wins 17-13 In rivalry games like this, you can forget about what has happened leading up to this contest. A big reason why I picked Michigan State to beat Michigan is that I knew that the Spartans would show up and play their best game of the year. They always do against Michigan. While I still don't think Kyle Whittingham can get his team up for a rivalry game like he should be able to, I do think that Ryan Day is in a particularly fragile state right now given the season that Ohio State has had and the current state of that program. Day seems to let the pressure get to him, and after the UCLA game, I feel like Michigan is playing with a "nothing to lose" mentality. Because of that, I have the Wolverines squeaking out a 17-13 victory.

Here are our predictions for the game: Ohio State vs. Michigan predictions Joey Kaufman, Columbus Dispatch: Michigan 24, Ohio State 20 : It's felt like fool's gold in recent weeks to pick Ohio State to end its late-season slide, so there's hesitation to pull that lever. Michigan's offensive futility should make it easy to go chalk with the Buckeyes . It averages the second-fewest points per game among Power 4 teams and has vacillated between starting Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback. But the Wolverines don't need to score much with a suffocating defense. They also have a bit of momentum after an upset of unbeaten UCLA last weekend. The vibes just seem better in Ann Arbor, which might matter the most with only bragging right at stake. Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 16 : I went back and forth on this one before deciding that Michigan's offense is simply too anemic to pull off a win in Ohio Stadium. The Wolverines rank 130th in first downs, 128th in passing yards and 99th in rushing yardage per game. On the flip side, UM's defense, ranked ninth nationally, is the most reliable piece on either team, so if the Wolverines can hold OSU to 14 points they have a great chance at winning in Columbus for a third straight time. It likely comes down to which team's head and heart are into a game where the only thing on the line is bragging rights. Brianna Mac Kay, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 21, Michigan 17 : Ohio State's offense with Luke Fahey at quarterback has shown flashes of promise, primarily before the defense put the Buckeyes in a deficit across the past four games. If the defense can keep Michigan under its season average of 18.3 points per game, which ranks 129th in the country, the offense should be able to put together enough momentum to finish the season with a win over the Wolverines. Dan Aulbach, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 : We finally get to see what happens when a stoppable force meets a moveable object. On the one hand, Michigan has the same starting quarterback as last year's edition of the rivalry, but Bryce Underwood has severely underperformed his expectations. Michigan's offense is lethargic, but Ohio State's defense has allowed 30-plus points in three of its last four games. Michigan's defense is elite (ninth in scoring defense), but so is Jeremiah Smith . The Buckeyes proved earlier in the year they can play and win against a defense-first team in Iowa, so I'll reluctantly pick the Buckeyes. Does it really matter all that much on a national scale? Yeah, it's getting stronger thanks to the consistent success of head coach Jeff Brohm at Louisville, and with Will Stein turning Kentucky into a rising power. The Wildcats might have slipped out of the CFP Top 25, but they've been in the mix over the last several weeks. Louisville is currently No. 19, and it might be the best ACC team available in the bowl process. Louisville vs Kentucky: Quick Hits Louisville has won six straight since losing back-to-back ACC games in late September. The 30-27 loss to Wake Forest was the difference between playing for the ACC Championship and finishing third in the conference. Kentucky started 7-1 but lost three straight. It's a win a way from this being the program's best season since 2021. Louisville won 41-0 last year, but Kentucky is 5-2 in the last seven meetings. That was part of the puzzle when the team was rolling, with 18 takeaways in the first eight games. There has been just one over this last three-game losing streak. Start forcing mistakes again, and the overall production will follow. UK quarterback Kenny Minchey has to crank up the big plays. All three Louisville losses came when the defense got hit by a slew of deep shots – Wake Forest, NC State, and Ole Miss all averaged over nine yards per throw. In Will Stein's head coaching debut, the Cats started league action on a high note and appeared to be on their way to Atlanta for the SEC championship game. But UK was outscored by a combined 83-34 in consecutive losses to Tennessee, Florida and Missouri. Turnovers and empty red-zone trips spelled trouble for Kentucky in its most recent loss, a 28-14 defeat against the Tigers. Kentucky ranks among the top two in the SEC (and the top 20 in the FBS) this season in both fewest total penalties and fewest penalty yards. Louisville is nowhere close to that in either department. With the Wildcats lacking upper hands elsewhere, their discipline is one area they should be able to hang their hat on this weekend. He also has a strong group of talented receivers around him and two explosive running backs beside him. But the Cards' six-game winning streak is equally due to their defense showing great improvement and getting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. A high-powered offense and much-improved defense will spell trouble for Will Stein and his stumbling Wildcats squad in Stein's first game on the other side of the Governor's Cup rivalry. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 28, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky hopes to snap a three-game losing streak and avoid losing a third straight game to Louisville. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. By Michael Harrison in College Football Published: November 28, 2026 at 9:15 am EST The Louisville Cardinals enter this instate battle riding a six-game winning streak, while the Kentucky Wildcats have dropped three straight Lincoln Kienholz and Isaac Brown give the visitors a massive statistical edge on the ground and through the air Read below for my top Governor's Cup Picks for this Saturday rivalry clash The college football slate brings an intense instate rivalry to the forefront as the Louisville Cardinals travel to Lexington to battle the Kentucky Wildcats. These two programs are trending in drastically opposite directions. Louisville sits at a commanding 8-3 after rattling off six straight victories, while Kentucky has stumbled to 7-4 on the heels of three consecutive SEC losses. Rivalry games naturally invite heavy public action, but finding the true edge requires looking past the emotion of the matchup. Let's dive into the trenches and break down the board to find the best value. Governor's Cup Picks When isolating my favorite Governor's Cup Picks, I always look for structural mismatches in the trenches. The market is hanging a tight number, but I see a clear path to cashing. Louisville -2.5 I am laying Louisville -2.5 with the visitors here. Louisville's ground and pound attack is simply too relentless for a reeling defense to handle for four quarters. Louisville vs Kentucky Prediction Louisville wins outright and covers the short spread in a clock-draining, physical battle. A Louisville defense allowing just 128.1 rushing yards per game should make it tough for Kentucky's offensive line to keep the Wildcats ahead of the chains. If the run game stalls, Minchey could face more third-and-long situations, and that is exactly how a road favorite wins in a hostile environment. The visitors have offensive firepower that the home team simply cannot match right now. Back the road favorite to hoist the trophy and end their regular season on a seven-game winning streak. Quarterback & Rushing Mismatch Louisville dominates the offensive metrics, averaging 38.6 points and 462.8 total yards per game. Kentucky manages just 27.0 points and 376.4 yards per contest by comparison. Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has been highly efficient, racking up 2,739 passing yards and 20 touchdowns with just four interceptions. His production outshines Wildcats signal-caller Kenny Minchey, who has tallied 2,448 yards and 15 touchdowns with four interceptions. The ground game is where Louisville truly separates themselves from the pack. Isaac Brown has chewed up 834 rushing yards at a blistering 7.0 yards per carry, eclipsing CJ Baxter's 610 yards for the home squad. Louisville's ground and pound approach averages 207.9 rushing yards per game, compared to just 153.8 rushing yards per game for Kentucky. That quarterback and rushing mismatch allows the visitors to dictate the tempo and control the field position battle. Alongside Isaac Brown, the visitors lean heavily on Keyjuan Brown, who has added 672 rushing yards while also averaging 7.0 yards per carry. That two-headed monster makes it nearly impossible for opposing defenses to catch a breather. Kentucky counters with Jason Patterson supporting Baxter in the backfield, but his 504 rushing yards simply don't provide the same explosive leverage. home.blurb: Wildcats fans are hopeful Moreno will be available for Friday’s game against Wichita State, but his long-term health remains the priority as the season continues. With Moreno’s status still uncertain, Kentucky will need its other frontcourt players to step up if the sophomore center is unable to return against Wichita State. Kentucky basketball has stumbled out of the gate. Here’s a look at the Wildcats’ best-case scenario, worst-case scenario, and updated season prediction. For Kentucky Basketball , it feels like when it rains, it pours, and the struggles continue to pile up for the Wildcats. Kentucky has struggled against weaker opponents; along with that, it has suffered blowout losses against some of the better teams on its schedule. Now, the Wildcats could be without one of their most important players as they look to get the season back on track. On Sunday, Matt Jones of Kentucky Sports Radio reported that sophomore center Malachi Moreno had entered concussion protocol after an Indiana player dove on him during Kentucky’s loss to the Hoosiers. Moreno hit his head on the floor during the play and was unlikely to play in Friday’s matchup against Wichita State. Although Moreno remained in the game against Indiana, head coach Mark Pope provided an update on the sophomore big man during his radio show on Tuesday, explaining that Moreno began experiencing concussion symptoms on Saturday. “He’s doing good,” Pope said on his radio show. “He kind of got a whole 270 pounds landed on his head, and kind of started after the game, and then especially, really the next day, started showing some symptoms. “So we put him in concussion protocol, and he’s responded really, really well, and so we’re hopeful that he’ll be back sooner rather than later because he’s playing so well.” For Kentucky, losing Moreno for multiple games would be a significant setback, especially considering how productive he has been this season. The sophomore center is averaging 13.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks, and 1.2 steals in 27.8 minutes per game. “He’s put up huge numbers, and he’s just playing at such a high level,” Pope continued. “It’s really important for us to get him back. We can’t wait till we get him back, and he’ll continue on with the terrific season.” All of your communities in one place. This is the title for the native ad More in Kentucky Wildcats Basketball

picks.headline: Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson
picks.blurb: Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer and his son Hunter speak with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney on the field before the Palmetto Bowl between at Memorial Stadium in Clemson on Saturday, November 30, 2024. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Jordan Kaye · The State Fri, November 27, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After finishing its SEC schedule with back-to-back losses to Arkansas and No. 1 Georgia, South Carolina (6-5) concludes the regular-season Saturday afternoon at Clemson (7-4). This will be the 123rd meeting between the Gamecocks and Tigers. Clemson leads the all-time series 74-44-4 and holds bragging rights after getting the 28-14 win over USC last year in Williams-Brice Stadium. The game is set to kick off at 3 p.m. and will be broadcast on ESPN2. And the betting public continues to back South Carolina. After opening as field-goal favorites, the Gamecocks are currently favored by 6 points. Those are some facts. Here are some thoughts. 1. South Carolina can't lose this game You'd quicker find a South Carolina fan who puts Will Muschamp on their Mount Rushmore than one who finds it acceptable losing to Clemson. But, certainly, during the late 2010s, when the Tigers were competing for national titles, it was a stretch to expect a Gamecock win. This year has been different. Ever since LSU used Clemson as its Week-1 cupcake, rolling to a 41-point win, South Carolina fans began salivating over the thought of a Spurrier-esque whooping on Nov. 28. This is the worst Clemson team in at least 16 years, and there's no reason the Gamecocks shouldn't take full advantage. That sentiment has changed a bit over the past few weeks as the Gamecocks have scored a combined 12 points against Arkansas and Georgia while Clemson looked competent in last week's win over Duke, sparked by the play of third-string quarterback Trent Pearman. Pearman has all the makings of a rivalry hero. He's the son of former Clemson assistant Danny Pearman, grew up around the Carolina-Clemson rivalry and will likely play the last two football games of his life before taking a normal-person job. He's the type of guy announcers gush over for hours as they show baby pictures of him in Clemson gear and tell us 15 times how it's "in his blood." "I can work a 9 to 5 the rest of my life," Pearman said this week. "This week is all about Clemson-South Carolina." It's up to the Gamecocks to make Saturday a nightmare for Pearman, to make it clear to every person watching why he was the Tigers' third-string option who's only playing because the other two got hurt. It's hard to imagine the embarrassment for South Carolina if it lost to this Clemson team, and the offseason ramifications that would ensure. No, not Shane Beamer getting fired . That's not happening, regardless of the result. But no staff change could be ruled out. No recruiting flip would be off the table. Nothing would be secure. That would make for a miserable offseason filled and real doubt about the future of the program. A win salvages optimism, especially if it's followed by a bowl victory. Folks in Columbia won't be — and shouldn't be — satisfied with eight wins, but it would be something to rally behind as the Gamecocks push to make the 24-team playoff next year. 2. LaNorris Sellers' decision looms After talking with three sources who would have knowledge of the situation, there is consensus that LaNorris Sellers has not made a decision about his plans for the 2027 season yet. Perhaps that's to be expected. He can sit down after the season and get a better feel for where he'd be projected to go in the NFL Draft if he wanted to declare. If we consider the reports that Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor is reportedly getting $7.5 million to return to Starkville next year and assume a Sellers contract would be in the same ballpark, it would be financially wise for him to return to college ... unless he's for sure going to be a first-round NFL Draft pick. Coming back would also give him another chance to play with his brother, USC receiver Jayden Sellers, who missed all season with an injury. And, well, many NFL Draft insiders have noted that Sellers would benefit from another year in college, especially if he can work with OC Kendal Briles again. Remember, the Gamecocks have had three different offensive coordinators in Sellers' three seasons as a starter. "LaNorris Sellers, there is a strong opinion in NFL scouting circles … that he will be back in school next year," draft analyst Todd McShay , who spent 17 years working at ESPN, said on his podcast in November. "That he absolutely needs to for his development." While Sellers' put together a monstrous highlight montage during the Gamecocks' four-game winning streak this season — remembered most by touchdown runs against Tennessee and Texas A&M — he was wildly inconsistent during the first month of the season and has been dealing with an ankle injury for much of the last three weeks. One can only imagine what Beamer would give for Sellers to return. Everything becomes so much easier if No. 16 comes back. Retaining Briles, whose name has been mentioned for the TCU head coaching job. Keeping your signing class intact. Attracting transfers. Talking with boosters. Garnering excitement about 2027. Hope becomes easy. Lose Sellers and, boy, the Gamecocks are in for a stressful offseason. 3. Home woes are bizarre The home team has not won the Palmetto Bowl since 2018, a stat that becomes harder to fathom as it continues to grow. While Carolina and Clemson didn't play in 2020, the road team has won the last six matchups in this rivalry. How rare is that? Well, we looked through the history of every SEC's teams rivalries (Alabama-Auburn, Florida-Florida State, etc.) and couldn't find another instance of six-straight road rivalry wins. The only time another rivalry has even come close in the last 80-plus years was Georgia-Georgia Tech about a decade ago. From 2013 to 2017 (five matchups), the road team was victorious in "Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate." "I think that's really, really hard to (win on the road) in a rivalry game," Beamer said, "so it's really fascinating to me that the road team has been able to do it so many consecutive games." The Carolina-Clemson road streak will be broken eventually. The Gamecocks hope it's not until next year. 4. Don't let this game come down to a kick While South Carolina's sophomore kicker Malik Orsan — a Southeast Missouri State transfer who enrolled this summer — has been solid as a first-year starter, hitting 13 of 17 field-goal attempts (including two from beyond 50), he will not be the best leg on Saturday. Clemson junior Nolan Hauser is arguably the best kicker in America, a Lou Groza Award finalist who tied the single-season NCAA record last week with his 31st made kick. He is 31 for 34 this season, including 15 of 18 from beyond 40 yards. South Carolina has to ensure this game is not close enough to be decided by kickers. 5. The playoff isn't a guarantee There are some college football plans who hear the words "24-team playoff" and think every team in the SEC is going to earn a bid. Heck, every SEC fan base is going to expect to be in that playoff come 2027. But, as this Gamecocks' season proved, it's not that easy. South Carolina would not have made the 24-team playoff this year. The Gamecocks have only been inside the Top 25 of the College Football Playoff Rankings on selection day three times in the last decade, and only twice under Beamer (2022 and 2024). Yes, Gamecock fans will rightfully rejoice if/when South Carolina makes the playoff. But the sting of the previous season is going to be that much worse if it's on the outside looking in. PREDICTION: South Carolina 20, Clemson 16
