Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

Here's your gameday guide for Clemson vs. South Carolina, including a score prediction for the 123rd edition of the in-state rivalry game. Clemson vs. South Carolina game, TV info Who: Clemson (7-4, 5-3 ACC) vs. South Carolina (6-5, 4-5 ACC) When: 3 p.m. Saturday Where: Memorial Stadium in Clemson Broadcast crew: Clay Matvick, Rocky Boiman, Marilyn Payne Stream: Via ESPN or the ESPN app Clemson radio: 105.5 FM in the Clemson area ( see full affiliate list ) South Carolina radio: 107.5 FM in the Columbia area ( see full affiliate list ) Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 110 or 249 Series history: Clemson leads 74-44-4 and won last meeting Clemson vs. South Carolina betting odds South Carolina is a six-point road favorite at Clemson, per the VegasInsider consensus betting line. The Gamecocks opened as a 3.5-point favorite last weekend, and the point spread has steadily ticked up in favor of USC. South Carolina being favored at Clemson is a rarity: Per BetIQ historical data, Saturday will mark only the third time it's happened since 1996 (2008, 2010). ESPN's Football Power Index gives South Carolina a 55.6% chance of winning. Clemson injury updates Starting cornerback Elliot Washington II missed the Duke game with an upper-body injury, and his status for Saturday is unclear, per coach Dabo Swinney. Same for starting slot receiver Tyler Brown, who's missed three games with an ankle injury. As a reminder, the Tigers are starting former walk-on quarterback Trent Pearman for a second-straight game because of injuries to starting quarterback Tait Reynolds (season-ending torn meniscus) and top backup Christopher Vizzina (concussion). South Carolina injury updates The Gamecocks should get two starters back against Clemson and possibly a third, according to coach Shane Beamer. Beamer said on his radio show that receiver Mazeo Bennett and edge rusher Anthony Addison are back in practice after missing the Georgia game. Injured defensive back Judge Collier could also return. Beamer said starting quarterback LaNorris Sellers (who returned vs. Georgia after missing the Arkansas game) is still managing an ankle injury but feels good. Weather forecast for Clemson, SC After a rainy week in South Carolina, AccuWeather projects a mostly clear Saturday in Clemson with a high of 60 degrees, "plenty of sun" and an 8% chance of rain. Final thoughts, score prediction The last time the home team won a game in this rivalry series was 2018, when Clemson beat South Carolina in a 56-35 shootout at Memorial Stadium. Swinney's Tigers were undefeated, marching toward a second national championship in three years. USC was in Year 3 of the Will Muschamp era. The fact the road team has won six straight games since that day speaks to the true 50-50 nature of this rivalry – especially since Shane Beamer started at South Carolina in 2021 and Clemson, the very same season, began a noticeable downward slide. South Carolina is favored by six points on Saturday. That feels about right. Yes, the Gamecocks are coming off back-to-back losses and have a worse record. But they've played a much tougher schedule, and they have the better quarterback. Friday's win at Duke proved that Clemson isn't throwing in the towel after losing its top two quarterbacks. The Tigers have good talent on defense, and their coaching staff did an excellent job maximizing the strengths of Pearman and Chris Denson. But it would take another perfect storm for an undermanned Clemson team to pull this off. The Tigers have lost nine of their last 11 home games against Power 4 teams, and Sellers, you may recall, has a pretty good track record in Death Valley. The former Clemson offensive lineman expects the Tigers to close the regular season with a second straight upset after winning 20-10 at Duke last Friday. "With all that said, Clemson is about to whip that ass," Mac Lain said. "I cannot wait to see this. The Tigers are going to win this thing." Fellow ACC analyst Kelly Gramlich also picked Clemson, though she sounded a little less certain about how this one plays out. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game. picks.headline: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s rivalry matchup vs South Carolina
picks.blurb: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s rivalry matchup vs South Carolina - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Staff score predictions for Clemson’s rivalry matchup vs South Carolina Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Clemson has won nine of its last 11 games against South Carolina, but you'd have a hard time convincing anyone who made the trip to Death Valley for the last two Palmetto Bowls there. The Gamecocks spoiled the afternoon for Clemson fans in 2022 and again in 2024. On Saturday, the Tigers get another shot at beating their rival in front of a home crowd. Clemson (7-4) found a way to win with Trent Pearman and Chris Denson sharing quarterback duties last week at Duke. Jarvis Green did much of the work on the ground, picking up 84 yards on 16 carries, but it was the two quarterbacks who got the Tigers into the end zone. Pearman scored from 9 yards out in the third quarter, and Denson added a 7-yard touchdown in the fourth to help put away the Blue Devils, 20-10. The pair combined for 122 rushing yards, and Pearman threw for another 164 in his first start. South Carolina (6-5) needs more out of its own quarterback after No. 1 Georgia held the Gamecocks to six points in Columbia. LaNorris Sellers finished with 87 yards passing, threw an interception and managed just 24 yards on nine carries. How often Clemson can get him on the ground Saturday figures to have plenty to do with whether the Tigers keep the Palmetto Bowl trophy after last year's 28-14 win in Columbia. Kickoff for the 123rd meeting is set for 3 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Here's how our Clemson Wire staff sees Saturday's rivalry game playing out in Death Valley. Alex Turri: Clemson 27, South Carolina 17 Nov 20, 2026; Durham, North Carolina, USA; Duke Blue Devils linebacker Nick Morris Jr. (7) attempts to tackle Clemson Tigers quarter back Trent Pearman (14) during the third quarter at Wallace Wade Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images Not only am I predicting a Clemson win today, but barely by double digits. The Tigers' home field advantage has been nearly nonexistent of late, but that should change today. There's just too much at stake. I feel Trent Pearman and Chris Denson will bring enough of a spark to score points, while the defense swarms South Carolina and quarterback LaNorris Sellers. Give me Clemson to win as dogs. Steve Holley: Clemson 20, South Carolina 23 Both head coaches desperately (capital D) need a win in this game. Home field advantage should favor Clemson, but the Tigers have been, uh, less than impressive at Memorial Stadium since 2024. They've lost nine of their last 11 home games against Power Four opponents. South Carolina looked really bad in back-to-back 34-6 losses, but I never expect teams to be "mailing it in" in rivalries this big. As fun as Clemson's upset win over Duke was behind Trent Pearman and Chris Denson, I'm not sure I really see it happening again. I could go either way with this pick, but Clemson's recent track record at Memorial Stadium really stands out to me. away.headline: Dabo Swinney Drops Sobering Injury Update Ahead of South Carolina Showdown
away.blurb: Clemson emerged from Friday night’s 20-10 road victory over Duke largely unscathed, though veteran quarterback Christopher Vizzina remains ruled out ahead of Saturday’s regular-season finale against rival South Carolina at Memorial Stadium. “ Injury wise, we came through it pretty good, so that was a positive,” Swinney said. “Hopefully everybody that played in the game will be able to keep going and finish this thing up strong. Nothing coming out of the game that was too worrisome, and then hopefully w e’ll get a couple guys back as well.” While Swinney is hopeful that everyone who suited up against Duke will be available—and that a few injured players could return—Vizzina will not be among them. The veteran signal-caller continues to recover from a severe concussion sustained late in Clemson’s 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech. With Vizzina sidelined and Tait Reynolds already out for the season following knee surgery, Clemson has turned to fifth-year senior Trent Pearman, who led the Tigers (7-4) past Duke in his first career start. Dabo Swinney Drops Sobering Injury Update Ahead of South Carolina Showdown Unlock the latest Heavy on Clemson news — direct to your inbox. During his Sunday evening teleconference, Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging assessment of his roster’s overall health following the win over the Blue Devils. “Oh, no, no, no, he’s nowhere near being back,” Swinney said. “I don’t think people realize how severe that was. He definitely will not be back.” Vizzina was taken to a hospital for precautionary evaluations after suffering the injury against Georgia Tech. Although tests on his neck and spine came back clear, significant concussion symptoms have persisted, capping an injury-marred 2026 campaign that has also included a broken arm and an ankle injury. “Again, it just breaks my heart for him,” Swinney said. “He was healthy for one game and two series of the second game, and outside of that, he’s … between the broken arm, the ankle, and now the concussion, it’s been a tough year.” The severity of his symptoms prevented Vizzina from participating in team activities last week, though Swinney hopes the quarterback can rejoin his teammates off the field during game week. “He couldn’t really even be around last week with the symptoms he was dealing with,” Swinney said. “Hopefully he’ll be able to be back and be in meetings and stuff this week, and finish up with these guys.” Saturday’s rivalry matchup against South Carolina is scheduled for a 3 p.m. kickoff on ESPN2. Clemson, which has lost its last two home games against the Gamecocks, enters the contest as a 4.5-point underdog according to FanDuel Sportsbook. South Carolina being favored at Clemson is a rarity: Per BetIQ historical data, Saturday will mark only the third time it's happened since 1996 (2008, 2010). More Videos The Clemson Tigers will face the South Carolina Gamecocks in their regular-season finale this Saturday , but they may have to do it without one of their top weapons. Wide receiver Tyler Brown has missed three straight games with an ankle injury, and his status for South Carolina seems up in the air. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney briefly discussed Brown during his weekly radio show on Monday, and he didn't seem to have much of an update. All Swinney had to say was that Brown was "still working his way back, so we'll see." That doesn't exactly sound too promising. Brown has caught 36 passes for 332 yards in eight games this season, representing a solid bounce-back year for the senior playmaker who was largely invisible two campaigns in a row for the Tigers. Brown arrived at Clemson in 2023 and actually got off to a terrific start, hauling in 52 receptions for 531 yards and four touchdowns. It has been a rough go for the 21-year-old ever since. Then, last year, Brown managed just 22 grabs for 191 yards. Brown has not reached the end zone since his debut campaign, and while that has a whole lot to do with him falling behind T.J. Moore and Bryant Wesco on the depth chart, it's fair to say that more was expected from him after his initial showing. He certainly appeared to be on a positive trajectory this season, but the ankle injury he sustained a few weeks ago has certainly thrown a wrench into things. Clemson was able to win without Brown last Friday, coming through with a surprising 20-10 victory over the Duke Blue Devils on the road. Moore led the way with four catches for 68 yards in the win. Wesco added two receptions for 12 yards. The Tigers improved to 7-4 with the victory, but they'll be facing a south Gamecocks squad with a dangerous offense this weekend. Luckily for the Tigers, their defense has been phenomenal this season, so hopefully Clemson can hold LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense in check. We'll see if any positive developments occur for Brown during the week.

picks.source: USC Trojans On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: From a conference championship appearance, a playoff berth and a straight-up rivalry, there's a lot at stake for No. 15 USC Trojans' season finale vs. the No. 9 UCLA Bruins. Odds may be shifting the Trojans' way but these three factors can guarantee a upset victory. 1. Defense Flusters UCLA Quarterback Madden Iamaleava The Bruins might have Ty Dieffenbach listed as “probable,” but it could be more of a guise to avoid the outcome Florida State had in 2023. For now, Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava, is expected to start, and the Trojans' defense should be licking its chops. When the sophomore entered the game, he looked hesitant and unprepared. The result was a rough outing, failing to make a complete pass and rushing for negative yards. On top of his depth chart status at the start of the year, Iamaleava has little high school experience to lean on as well. Madden backed up Nico at Warren High (Downey, Calif.) from his freshman to sophomore year. He made a total of 17 appearances during that time, but it was a small sample size. Then in 2023, Madden became the full-time starter. In 13 games, he threw for 3,626 yards, 43 touchdowns and only four interceptions, per MaxPreps. He showed flashes of being a dynamic runner as well, rushing for 305 yards and three scores. A fallout at Warren led to a midseason transfer attempt to Long Beach Poly. Ultimately, Iamaleava did not play his senior year. Plus, the Bruins' offense has already been struggling under Dieffenbach – four interceptions in seven games, two of which came from Dieffenbach against Michigan in Week 12, No. 98 in points per trip inside the opponent’s 40-yard line and a lack of explosive plays despite having an excellent rushing attack. As great as coach Bob Chesney has been this season, it seems like a tall task to have the young Iamaleava ready on Nov. 28. Despite a slow start, USC’s defense came to play against a red-hot Maryland offense. Despite having a low pressure rate of 28 percent, the line was able to record four quarterback hits. The defensive front also disrupted the Terrapins’ run game with four tackles for loss (seven yards). More importantly, the secondary came away with three interceptions. With a lack of an outside threat, USC can focus on bringing the pressure from the interior and a blitzing nickelback. Desman Stephens II and Deven Bryant have done an excellent job leading the middle of the defense, and they will be huge in slowing down the Bruins' lead back, Wayne Knight. Taking all that into consideration, the Trojans defense can come away with three to four sacks and three turnovers in the contest. 2. Another Dominant Day on the Ground for Waymond Jordan and King Miller It appeared that Lincoln Riley was going to fall into old habits when trailing 14-13 to Maryland at halftime – get pass-happy, speed up the momentum and make questionable play calls. Fortunately, the USC offense got gritty with the run game, taking pressure off quarterback Jayden Maiava while providing an easy check-down option and milking the clock. The dynamic duo of Waymond Jordan and King Miller accounted for 140 of USC’s 184 rushing yards. Jordan – 18 carries, 70 yards, two touchdowns – looks healthy as ever, with his quick cuts and strong finishes. Miller – 10 carries for 70 yards – continues to shine as the explosive runner and is a huge plus as an easy pass option. It's also worth noting that Southern Cal is 8-1 when they rush for 100-plus yards and 0-2 when they rush for less than 100 – both of which were on the road. Riley has seemed to grow fond of the 12-personnel look and two-back backfield, which only opens up the passing game when the backfield duo is rolling. He needs to lean on it once again. Going against the Bruins' defense won't be an easy task, as the unit is No. 6 in rushing yards allowed per game (88.5) and No. 4 in yards per rush (2.7), but if USC can sustain drives with the run, they can tire out and punish this defense. With Miller as the lead rusher this time around, the two will combine for 120-plus yards and account for two scores on the day. 3. Double Digit Victory for the USC Trojans USC has won by double digits five times this season. While all five were at home, the Trojans won’t be dealing with the away-game narrative at the Rose Bowl. Similar to the Ohio State game, the defense will keep everything in front of them while flustering a young, backup quarterback. The offense will be willing to play a smash-mouth game while getting the ball to wideout Trent Mosley for explosive plays for a final score of 35-17. home.headline: Why UCLA Football's Michigan Loss Is Extremely Concerning
home.blurb: For the first time all season, UCLA football is left grappling with a loss. The Bruins are in danger of spiraling. UCLA is still standing strong at 10-1, but the near and distant future is clouded with uncertainty for a few particular reasons after losing at Michigan. Ty Dieffenbach Could Miss Major Time On the first play of overtime, quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was carted off the field after suffering an apparent lower-body injury. Coach Bob Chesney did not provide a clear update postgame, as additional testing is needed to determine the severity of Dieffenbach's injury. Whatever the injury is revealed to be, the fact that Dieffenbach was carted off the field is a five-alarm fire for UCLA. He had led his team to an undefeated month and a half as the starting quarterback. The Bruins are now likely down to Madden Iamaleava, their third-string quarterback. Iamaleava was 0-1 passing today with two carries for -1 yard. Run Game Was Beatable, Which Has Not Happened Often For the first time this season, UCLA was held to just 2.5 yards per carry on 42 attempts. It was an ugly day for a usually dominant ground game. Michigan's shifty 4-2-5 front was able to consistently rush the passer and hawk to the football, even with extra defensive backs on the field in some run situations. The Wolverines didn't fare all that better, but that's not much consolation given how poorly Michigan's offense has performed throughout the 2026 campaign. The Bruins haven't been held to 16 points in a game since the 2025 season finale at USC. On the subject of the Trojans, next week's matchup has now become a lot more complicated. Big Ten Title Hopes Are Suddenly in Jeopardy The loss at Michigan means UCLA probably needs to beat USC , without Dieffenbach, to clinch a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. If Oregon and Iowa win next week but the Bruins lose, they won't earn a spot. There is also a scenario in which UCLA loses, four results go against it, and then the Bruins are left watching from the couch. The simplest answer is that a Bruins win means they are heading to Indianapolis. But can UCLA rekindle its magic with quarterback No. 3, particularly after a sluggish outing by the whole offense? The answer to that question will directly dictate whether the Bruins can reach the conference title game, let alone host a College Football Playoff game. At the end of October, the Sooners were 4-4 with a win over No. 1 Texas but also two one-score victories over New Mexico and Mississippi State (without Kamario Taylor ), losses to Michigan and Kentucky , and a blowout at the hands of Georgia . But since then, OU has won three in a row over Florida (holding the Gators to seven points), Ole Miss and Texas A&M . While the Sooners are almost certainly outside the College Football Playoff field, an 8-4 finish despite persistent offensive struggles would have to be considered a success for Brent Venables. New offensive coordinator Jason Witten, a former NFL star, replaced Ben Arbuckle, and the offense has run pretty cleanly under him. Although scoring hasn't increased, the unit has looked a bit more organized, and quarterback John Mateer has been used much more effectively, especially with his legs. Venables' defense has finally taken root in Norman. OU ranks in the top 10 nationally in Success Rate allowed (36.5%), Points Per Scoring Opportunity and Havoc. The Sooners have held their last three opponents to a combined 31 points, although we've seen two major lapses against South Carolina (42 points) and at Georgia (41). The offense put the defense in bad positions in both games, but the Gamecocks connected on 84- and 79-yard touchdowns, and the Bulldogs scored two offensive TDs from 35-plus yards out. That has been a side effect of Venables' aggressive style, but against this schedule, it has resulted in some pretty costly outings. Oklahoma scored 25 against South Carolina, just its second game with 24-plus points against an opponent not named UTEP . Tackling has been a major issue, as Sooner defenders have whiffed on over 18% of their attempts, worse than all but four teams in 2026. Missouri Tigers Betting Preview: Offense on One Leg Losing superstar back Ahmad Hardy before the season began was an enormous blow to this team. He has since returned to the field, but in an extremely limited capacity, and he's visibly nowhere near 100% — in four games, he's averaged 3.8 yards on 13 carries. He's not even walking out of the tunnel comfortably. It's a real shame and something that's held Mizzou's offense back on multiple occasions. Quarterback Austin Simmons has been a bona fide hit in the transfer portal. The 6-foot-4 lefty has 25 touchdown passes against just four interceptions and has proven to be an exceptional downfield passer despite drops on 9% of his targets (14th-most in the FBS). But the Tigers can't run the ball consistently and get no explosiveness from that phase of the game. Against Ole Miss and Texas — teams with dangerous pass rushes and good secondaries — the offense shut down completely. Simmons shows terrific escapability in the pocket, but without an effective ground game to alleviate the pressure, defenses have been able to bear down on him. Mizzou's defense has done a good job controlling opposing offenses and keeping the lid on the field. It ranks inside the top 30 nationally in explosive play rate and the top 10 in turnovers generated. The Tigers also limit success in the red zone, holding opponents to the 13th-worst efficiency inside the 20. But like the offense, this unit has been exposed. Georgia just put up 48 points thanks to three quick strikes early in the game. Ole Miss rushed for over 250 yards, and Arch Manning found his most success against an SEC foe with 300 passing yards (no interceptions). The good news for the future of this team is that Simmons will be back for his final season in 2027. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Dave Neal, Cole Cubelic and Tori Petry) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know COLUMBIA, Mo. — Oklahoma (7-4, 5-3 SEC) will look to extend their win streak to four as they head to Faurot Field to take on Missouri (7-4, 4-4 SEC). The Sooners have strung together three straight wins over Florida, Ole Miss, and Texas A&M after alternating wins and losses in each of their first nine games this year, the longest such streak in program history to open a season. The Sooners' 10th opponent out of 12 this fall will be the Missouri Tigers, who were either ranked or receiving votes in at least one major poll at kickoff. Only Oklahoma's opener against UTEP and last week's opponent, Texas A&M, were not ranked or receiving votes. This will be the 99th meeting between the two former conference rivals . The series is 68-25-5 in Oklahoma's favor, including a 9-2 record in the last 11 meetings, 21-3 in the last 24 meetings, and 23-7 in the last 30 meetings in Columbia. OU is 17-6 all-time against ranked Missouri teams. The Sooners and Tigers have played each other as members of the Missouri Valley Intercollegiate Athletic Association, the Big Seven, the Big Eight, the Big 12, and now in the SEC. Under Sooners head coach Brent Venables , OU is 1-1 against Missouri. The Tigers got the best of Oklahoma in their first meeting as SEC institutions in 2024, with a 30-23 win in Columbia. Then in 2025, Oklahoma returned the favor with a 17-6 victory in Norman. Since last season, OU has won five of its last six SEC road games (excluding a 27-24 win over No. 1 Texas in Dallas in 2024), including wins at Mississippi State and No. 25 Florida in 2026 and wins at South Carolina, No. 14 Tennessee, and No. 4 Alabama in 2025. Oklahoma's offense has found new life this month since Jason Witten was promoted from tight ends coach to interim offensive coordinator. Under Witten, the Sooners have averaged 25 points per game. OU's offense has done a much better job of playing complementary football, controlling the clock, running the football, and making life easier on the defense by keeping them off the field. As a result, the Sooners' defense has allowed an average of just 10 points per game over their last three contests. With only five drives of 10 or more plays in the first five games of the season, Oklahoma has had 18 such drives in the last six games. This includes a 20-play, 12:45 drive for a touchdown against Florida, the Sooners' longest such drive since 1972 and the longest by any SEC team this season. Third-down conversions have improved from 37% in the first eight games to 52% under Witten, and time of possession is averaging 36:08 per game (fifth in the country and best among Power Four teams during the stretch). Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer has played better in the Sooners' last three games than in the previous nine, scoring three touchdowns on 335 total yards in last week's 28-7 win over Texas A&M and three touchdowns on 337 total yards in the previous three games. His three highest rushing totals of the season have come in those last three games (56 yards at Florida, 70 vs. Ole Miss, 66 vs. Texas A&M). He has rushed for 192 of his 337 rushing yards in the three games Witten has called the plays. This includes both of his rushing touchdowns this season, running behind the same five offensive linemen in each of those three games: Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris. Isaiah Sategna III leads the Sooners in receiving with 56 catches for 722 yards and five touchdowns, averaging 102.3 all-purpose yards per game, including two punt-return touchdowns. Mackey Award semifinalist Rocky Beers is averaging 56.9 yards receiving per game, most in the SEC among tight ends, with five touchdowns, most by an OU tight end since Mark Andrews in 2017. Lloyd Avant, Tory Blaylock and Jonathan Hatton Jr. are contributing on the ground for the Sooners. Missouri (5-1 at home, 2-3 on the road) started the season 5-1 and rose to No. 13 in the AP poll before losing three of their last five games. However, they most recently pulled off a 28-14 win against No. 16 Kentucky. The Tigers can rely on left-handed quarterback Austin Simmons . This season, Simmons has thrown for 2,693 yards, 25 touchdowns, and four interceptions. Mizzou's backfield is loaded with 1,200-yard rusher Jamal Roberts and 2025 All-American Ahmad Hardy, who is returning from a leg injury. The Tigers' offense also includes dynamic receivers in Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode. Missouri has had a great season defensively, leading the SEC in turnover margin. However, the Tigers allow a lot of passing yards and have given up quite a few explosive plays this season. That means Mateer and Witten can get things done on offense if Oklahoma can protect the football as they have in the last five games, with just two total giveaways. The Sooners' defense is made up of all homegrown players who started their college careers in Norman. All 15 players who have started at least one game this season play on defense. Oklahoma's defense is top-20 in the country in third-down defense (27.4%, No. 3), first downs allowed (14.3 per game, No. 3), passing defense (163.1 ypg, No. 7), red-zone defense (72.0%, No. 8), total defense (284.6 ypg, No. 12), sacks (2.8 per game, No. 17), and scoring defense (17.9 ppg, No. 18). With Butkus Award semifinalist Owen Heinecke leading the Sooners' defense in tackles with 91, 11.5 for loss, as well as Kip Lewis, David Stone, and lockdown corner Courtland Guillory (36.2 passer rating allowed when targeted), Oklahoma will be looking to have a clean, tackling-focused, disciplined game in Columbia on Saturday.

How to watch MU When does Missouri football play OU this week? TV, kickoff details End of the line, where we'll see two old foes meet for the 99th time. Missouri football hosts Oklahoma this coming Saturday, Nov. 28, for its regular season finale in Columbia. The Tigers are currently ranked No. 23 in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings, and the Sooners are No. 17. The last game between these two teams on Faurot Field was a thriller. Mizzou scored 14 points in the final 63 seconds of the game to win the first reunion between the former Big Eight and Big 12 rivals. The Tigers (7-4, 4-4 SEC) are playing for a fourth straight season with eight or more regular season wins and a winning record in SEC play. Should MU beat the Sooners, Eli Drinkwitz's contract also will automatically be extended by one year. Oklahoma (7-4, 5-3) has won its last three games to right the ship on its season. The Sooners effectively shut Missouri's offense down in a 17-6 win last season in Norman. These teams, who first faced off in 1902, are playing for the 99th time Saturday. Here's what you need to know about Oklahoma before Saturday's regular-season finale: Oklahoma has committed to running struggling QB John Mateer Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer (10) runs with the ball during his team's 2025 game against Missouri at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. The Sooners have gotten out of their offensive rut by committing to running quarterback John Mateer, who was really struggling to begin this season. At the start of November, the Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and replaced him with interim play caller Jason Witten. The major change the Sooners have made is getting their quarterback going with his legs, and that's led to an uptick in overall production and fewer turnovers — a good combination. Mateer was averaging nine carries per game for 32 rushing yards per game. Since the OC change, he's taken an average of 13.3 carries for 71.3 yards on the ground per game. OU has averaged 161.3 yards of rushing offense per game in wins over Florida, Ole Miss and Texas A&M in November. The Sooners had only surpassed 161.3 rushing yards in two of their previous eight games. Mateer threw seven interceptions in the opening eight games of the year and fumbled five times. He's thrown one pick and had one fumble in the last three games. More: Missouri faces Oklahoma offense that's found new life in November What makes the OU defense consistently excellent? Brent Venables: Defensive play-caller in name only. "He's got a stylistic way that he calls defenses that he almost approaches it, to me, like an offensive coordinator does. He's not very defensive," MU coach Eli Drinkwitz said. "He's pretty offensive as a defensive coordinator, where he is setting the tone and taking the fight to you." Oklahoma, as tends to be the case, ranks among the better statistical defenses in the SEC this season. The Sooners rank fourth in the conference by allowing 284.6 yards of offense per game, including the best pass defense at 163.1 yards per game. The Sooners are on track to field a top-20 defense in FBS for total yards allowed per game for a third straight season — every year since joining the SEC. "I was speaking with somebody and they said the top 14 players on the Oklahoma defense all have played their entire career at Oklahoma and have been there the whole time," Drinkwitz said, "which gives you a foundation so that when you're walking through or showing this defense and you use terms like 'this is how we played it last year, this is what we did last time,' or they've seen that install, there's the repetition. There's the foundation of what they're going to do." Who are OU's top playmakers? Drinkwitz said Oklahoma has the "best defensive front that we've seen all year." The Sooners have nine different players with at least 3.5 tackles for loss this season. Eight different players have registered multiple sacks. Defensive tackle David Stone, who has 4.5 sacks from the interior, and experienced linebacker Owen Heinecke, who has 11.5 tackles for loss, are likely All-SEC picks. Most of Oklahoma's receiving production has come via two players: wide receiver Isaiah Sategna and tight end Rocky Beers. Sategna has caught 56 passes for 722 yards and five touchdowns, and he has also returned two punts for touchdowns this year. Beers has 49 catches for 626 receiving yards and five touchdowns, which leads SEC tight ends. Score prediction: Missouri 17, Oklahoma 14 More: Naeshaun Montgomery spent nights in the Mizzou locker room. No one's sleeping on him now. Oklahoma is as strong as always on the defensive side of the ball and has found something it can lean on with its offense. This has the makings of a game that comes down to the wire (and one that maybe looks a little ugly along the way). We'll give the Tigers the edge on their home field. picks.headline: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri
picks.blurb: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will No. 17 Oklahoma Finish the Regular Season With a Win at No. 23 Missouri?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will No. 17 Oklahoma Finish the Regular Season With a Win at No. 23 Missouri? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games College football live updates NBA Cup: Knockouts set Steelers roll without Rodgers Wrestler's stunning death Luka shoved by fan Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Jeremiah Newcombe (21) celebrates after a sack against Texas A&M. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 27, 2026 at 1:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads With seven straight November wins in their pocket dating back to last year, the Sooners have a chance to finish the season with nine wins. Not too bad, considering they were just 4-4 and limping to the finish line less than a month ago. Can interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten sustain enough of those quarter-eating, length-of-the-field possessions at Faurot Field to push the Sooners to their fourth straight victory and an 8-4 regular -season finish - and a 6-3 mark in Southeastern Conference play? The Tigers lost three of four games (to No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 7 Texas and No. 1 Georgia) before bouncing back with a big win over Kentucky in Columbia last week. Their defense isn't good, but their offense will score. Can the Sooners keep up? Final Score: Missouri 28, Oklahoma 27 Missouri represents another step up for Jason Witten and the OU offense to deal with. The Tiger defense is comparable, though different, than Texas A&M's unit, but the offense can actually put points on the board and assert pressure if the Sooners come up empty on possessions. Oklahoma's defense needs to have a good tackling day to get Missouri's offense behind the chains. That could help OU force turnovers, which the Tigers have not often given out throughout the year. Missouri can also rush the passer, which will be a big test for John Mateer's decision making. If he can get the ball out quickly, the Sooners will have a chance to make the plays on both sides of the ball to win a tight one. Final Score: Oklahoma 17, Missouri 16 Oklahoma looks like a totally different team than it did earlier in the year. The Sooners' defense is still one of the nation's best. And while the offense isn't a high-flying attack, it has improved significantly. The Sooners have averaged 25 points per game since they parted ways with Ben Arbuckle and promoted Jason Witten to be the interim offensive coordinator. OU's complementary brand of football has allowed the Sooners to climb to No. 17 in the College Football Playoff rankings - just a few weeks after the season seemed lost in late October. The Sooners will cap off their turnaround with an impressive road win against Missouri. Final Score: Oklahoma 31, Missouri 23 This matchup is extremely intriguing. Oklahoma's defense hasn't been tested in a major way over the last two games for various reasons - the weather vs. Ole Miss made it almost impossible for Trinidad Chambliss to push the ball through the air; and Texas A&M's offense was inept. But Missouri is a different animal. Jamal Roberts is probably the best running back the Sooners have faced this season; Austin Simmons has 25 touchdowns with just four interceptions through the air and the Tigers have one of the best receiver duos around in Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode. The secondary in particular will be tested in a way they haven't been since at least Texas. Oklahoma will need do tackle well defensively, make enough disruptive plays to keep Simmons out of rhythm, establish the run offensively and at least get enough explosive plays to keep the Tigers' defense honest. If they're able to do that, the Sooners have a good chance of escaping Columbia with their first win there since 2006. Final Score: Oklahoma 20, Missouri 17 Brady Trantham Jason Witten's offense has improved each week in terms of being able to perform more tasks and execute with consistency. Not to mention the subtle uptick in scoring with each outing and you have a Sooner offense that is playing with confidence for the first time in 2026. OU's balanced attack, with John Mateer's legs now a big part of the equation, proves too much for the Tigers' stout but leaky defense. Sooners force a few turnovers to make Missouri's final home game of the year a nightmare. away.headline: Friday night injury report for Oklahoma at Missouri
away.blurb: Oklahoma will be without at least seven players this week against Missouri. Wide receivers Trell Harris and Ivan Carreon, tight end Trynae Washington, offensive linemen Fred Hinton and Gunnar Allen, linebacker Taylor Heim, and defensive back Reggie Powers III have been listed as out this week. Powers' absence is by far the most important, as he was downgraded to out on Friday night. He's been OU's starter at Cheetah all season long, but he exited the Texas A&M win with an injury last week. Without him, the Sooners will be leaning on defensive back Jeremiah Newcombe and linebacker Cole Sullivan to step up and play a larger role in the defense against a very good Mizzou offense. Offensive lineman E'Marion Harris is still listed as doubtful to play this week. With his availability this week not looking likely, look for the Sooners to roll out a starting o-line five of Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and Ryan Fodje from left to right up front. Harris has been the season-long starter at right tackle, but Fodje, who is now off the injury report this week as of Thursday night, should step into that role, as he did last week when Harris was hurt. Best was also injured against the Aggies, but he did not appear on the injury report at all this week. Eddy Pierre-Louis filled in for him at left guard to finish last week's game. Two Sooners are now probable to play this week, in wide receiver Parker Livingstone and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu. While Ozowalu is a depth piece at the defensive end spot, Livingstone would be a boost to the wideout group if he's able to play. He's had a larger role in the offense with Jason Witten at the helm over the last three weeks. Additionally, running back Tory Blaylock is available to play this week, after previously appearing on the injury report. He led the Oklahoma RBs in carries last week. Missouri will have at least five players out this week. They'll be without running back Malae Fonoti, tight end Gavin Hoffman, offensive lineman Josh Atkins, EDGE Langden Kitchen, and cornerback Cameron Keys. Additionally, long-snapper Brett Le Blanc is listed as questionable on the Friday report. away.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Texas A&M injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting OL Ryan Fodje: GAME-TIME DECISION Fodje injured his ankle in the loss to Kentucky and has been sidelined ever since. He was ruled out early in weeks until last week, when he was listed as doubtful before ultimately being unavailable against Ole Miss. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. In the meantime, Heath Ozaeta has been anchoring that RG spot while Fodje has been out. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. He's been a regular on the availability report after being banged up since before the season even kicked off, but he has still missed only the opener. He was listed as probable most of this week. Replacement: Freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. will get touches whether Blaylock is available or not, but he should get even more if Blaylock is on the sidelines. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. CB Dezz Ricks: game-time decision Everything seems to be going right for the Oklahoma Sooners right now, including a shrinking injury report. The No. 22 Sooners host Texas A&M on Saturday in Norman for a reunion between two old Big 12 rivals. OU, at 6-4, is eyeing a three-game winning streak and just appeared in the CFP rankings for the first time this season after back-to-back ranked wins. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. It's not a long list, but there are still a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff. This is the closest we've been in five weeks to seeing Ryan Fodje on the football field. If Fodje returns today, it would be the first time this season the Sooners have their full starting offensive line healthy. Before his injury, Fodje had started every game but the season opener, during which he was also injured. He's listed as the starter at right guard, but he hasn't actually played there yet this season. He filled in for Michael Fausi at left tackle for the five games he was healthy. Washington has won in its last three, including a stunning victory last week against defending champion Indiana by the score of 27-24. Quarterback Demond Williams stole the show after not just throwing for 227 yards, but leading the team in rushing with a touchdown . Williams has gotten better as the season has progressed. He's avoided turning the ball over and has formed an elite chemistry with Chris Lawson and Dezmen Roebuck. Lawson has been a total beauty this season, averaging 15 yards per catch, and Roebuck is fresh off a game where he hauled in a season-high for receptions against Indiana. One part of this offense, though, that is completely ineffective is the Huskies' run game. Williams actually leads the team in rushing on just 3.9 yards per carry, while true freshman running back Brian Bonner Jr. has been a nonfactor for the most part. It largely makes Washington's offense predictable since it's so ineffective on the ground. It forces Williams to drop back even more, but his scrambling ability has helped create offense. This defense has been really strong for the most part. Safety Alex McLaughlin and linebacker Jacob Manu are tackling machines, but McLaughlin is tied for the lead with three interceptions and leads with eight PBUs. Both Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. are questionable, which could leave Brandon Smith as Oregon's bell-cow. Smith proved that he can handle the workload after rushing for 121 yards and two touchdowns against Michigan State . And this offense as a whole has played on another level after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer midseason. Dylan Raiola has done an admirable job once it was revealed that Dante Moore was no longer going to participate this season. Raiola has thrown only two interceptions this season, and both came in Week 6 against UCLA . I've always been impressed with how Raiola has played, even dating back to his Nebraska days, and, unfortunately, he couldn't make it work at his father's alma mater. But what better place is there to develop than Oregon? Wide receiver Dakorien Moore has clearly taken another step in his development, generating 23% of the Ducks' receptions, with 250 more receiving yards than the next receiver, Evan Stewart. Coming into this season, I was expecting Oregon's defense to be one of the more dominant defenses in college football. Starting the season definitely concerned me, but we're starting to see this program come back. Matayo Uiagalelei, who's ranked ninth in sacks, is just 1.5 sacks away from the school record. The Ducks also have one of the best secondaries in the country, featuring defensive backs Na'eem Offord and Ify Obidegwu, each with 11 PBUs, along with Koi Perich, one of the country's better tacklers. If either Davison or Hill is ready to go, then I do think Oregon pulls away. I would pay close attention closer near game time to make a strong choice. Arizona State safety Adrian Wilson crashed into Coleman, sending the 5-foot-6, 158-pound receiver toppling over. Medical personnel walked Coleman into the injury tent, where he remained for the remainder of the drive. The play was reviewed for targeting and upheld. Wilson is ejected from the game. Deion Imade on the Cowboy Radio Network reported Coleman emerged from the tent with a smile on his face and was attempting to convince OSU personnel he is able to continue playing. Coleman leads OSU against Arizona State with four receptions for 46 yards. OSU trails Arizona State 24-14 with 10:39 remaining in the third quarter.
